design.name: Interface test shank
design.description: A hypothetical 90 × 20 µm single shank with a 300 µm pointed tip and eight finite surface contacts. Neuropixels-inspired silhouette; dimensions and mixed contact sizes are a test design, not an optimized or manufactured device.

references.title: Jun et al. 2017 — Fully integrated silicon probes for high-density recording of neural activity
references.supports: Neuropixels single-shank inspiration; the original is 70 × 20 µm with a 10 mm shank, not this test geometry.

references.title: Steinmetz et al. 2021 — Neuropixels 2.0
references.supports: Slender shank and tapered tip inspiration; this test design does not reproduce the device.

references.title: COMSOL — Current Distribution, Boundary Elements
references.supports: Boundary integral conductor formulation; does not validate this implementation.

sampleDomain: At each contact: y=10,25,100 µm; x offsets 0,width/2,width; z offsets 0,height/2. All 8 contact lead fields.
limitations: The visible finite shaft is approximated electrically by an infinite insulating backing plane. No fields around its sides, back or tip are represented.
Floating inactive contacts have zero net current but may carry nonzero induced local panel currents.
Homogeneous isotropic resistive tissue; ideal conducting contact surfaces; no interface impedance, capacitance, noise or amplifier model.
No neural sample is accepted below 10 µm from the backing plane. Edge and surface fields are not reported.
Neural recording uses point transmembrane-current sources at compartment centers and the reciprocal finite-contact lead fields.
Numerical consistency and mesh checks do not establish real implant accuracy, tissue safety or biological selectivity.
independentConductorComparison: Not performed for this multi-contact configuration.
